Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-29
Start: 09:30 PDT
Duration: 42m
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lina Torres (Redwood CSM), Dr. Elena Morales (CTO, Cardinal Analytics), Michael Park (Lead ML Eng), Rita Singh (SRE), Tom Wu (Procurement)

Summary (auto): weekly POC readout focusing on latency/throughput contrast vs incumbent provider. Action items: exchange traces, run targeted microbench, schedule routing deep-dive.

[00:00] Ava (AE): All right good morning everybody, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — we got Elena, Michael, Rita, Tom from Cardinal, and Samir and I from Redwood. Hi.
[00:18] Dr. Elena: Morning, yeah thanks. We got a packed agenda, mostly about the numbers you sent last night.
[00:25] Ava: Great, let's jump in. Samir, do you want to give the 10k-foot on the results?
[00:30] Samir (SE): Yep, quick context: we re-ran the suite with the same model family you used with IncumbentAI — we matched sequence length at 2048 for the long-context runs, and 256 for the short ones. Baseline was IncumbentAI's "prod-fast" region. Key observed: p50 latency is comparable on short requests but p95/p99 on our hosted smallest batch runs was slightly higher by ~18-25 ms for the 256 context case. Throughput under sustained 90% CPU/GPU load we saw ~12% higher tokens/sec than baseline on quantized dedicated slots, but startup latency for cold KV warrants discussion.
[01:10] Michael (Customer): Hmm, the 18-25 ms at p95 is... not huge but noticeable in the UI. Can you reproduce with our traffic shape? Remember ours has heavy tail: many small queries with chat-like back-and-forth.
[01:24] Samir: Right, that's the tail we're seeing. My suspicion: our continuous-batching policy (we default to very low hold) plus prefix/KV cache warmup means early tokens have higher overhead until the KV is shared. Also kernel selection for the particular quantized path adds micro-sched jitter.
[01:42] Rita (SRE): Are those numbers from dedicated or hosted? We want to understand isolation — our security team prefers dedicated if latency improves.
[01:49] Ava: The p95 delta I mentioned was from hosted API runs with small concurrency. For dedicated GPU pools we were already seeing improvement in throughput vs baseline.
[01:58] Dr. Elena: Can you explain the KV warmup thing? That term sometimes gets lost in our architecture discussions.
[02:04] Samir: Sure — KV refers to the key-value cache (the KV cache for autoregressive decoding). If the request hits a shard that hasn't been warmed with the conversation prefix, the runtime needs to load caches or recompute parts. For multi-tenant hosted runs we saw a few ms of extra cost when the cache wasn't present. IncumbentAI's setup appears to have more aggressive pre-warming or sticky routing, so their p95 is slightly better on short-turn chat traffic.
[02:28] Michael: Is that something Redwood can tune without changing our app? We can't reshape traffic much.
[02:34] Samir: Yes — we can adjust routing to favor sticky sessions for chat flows, increase prefix caching TTL for your project, or configure dedicated slots so KV warmup happens once per slot. There's trade-offs though: sticky routing reduces statistical multiplexing and can raise unit-cost.
[02:48] Tom (Procurement): Cost is the headline for us — you mentioned dedicated had better tokens/sec, but what's the delta to the incumbent?
[02:54] Ava: Ballpark: in the microbench, dedicated quantized slots were 10-15% cheaper per 1M tokens than baseline when we optimized batching and quantization. We'll send a more exact pricing delta in the spreadsheet.
[03:06] Dr. Elena: Okay. Another area: tail-latency spikes during short bursts — what caused them?
[03:12] Samir: Two things: cold KV and routing fallbacks. For the debug run on 7/26 we had a few fallbacks to the general-purpose variant when a dedicated slot wasn't available, which shows up as latency jitter. We can set a fallback policy to prefer slightly slower-but-cheaper compatible variants or reserve a small burst pool.
[03:30] Michael: Could we do a canary where we pin 10% of traffic to dedicated slots as you recommended? See real user impact.
[03:36] Ava: Definitely — that aligns with our rollout playbook. We'll help set up a canary route and measure user-facing p95 over 72 hours.
[03:43] Rita: From SRE-side we need logs: end-to-end traces, GPU utilization, and the IncumbentAI baseline traces you compared against. Can you get us those?
[03:51] Samir: We can share Redwood's traces and the benchmark harness logs; for the baseline we asked you to send the vendor traces since we don't have access to Incumbent's internal telemetry.
[03:59] Michael: Yep, I'll export the vendor traces and a sample of 10k requests. Expect that by Monday.
[04:05] Ava: Great. On the quantization topic: we ran your model on two quant profiles — 4-bit hybrid and int8. Hybrid 4-bit gave best throughput at the cost of slightly worse p99 under long sequences. Int8 was more stable but slightly lower throughput.
[04:20] Dr. Elena: Stability matters more for us than raw throughput if it reduces re-try and user-visible errors.
[04:25] Samir: Then int8 path plus dedicated slot with prefix caching looks like the right sweet spot. We'll tune the fusion kernels and compile flags to squeeze more p95 out of it.
[04:36] Tom: Anything on security/compliance we should note? Our legal team asked specifically about audit logs and KMS.
[04:42] Ava: For Private deployments we have a VPC option, customer-managed KMS/HSM, and audit log retention; we also can produce a SOC 2 artifact pack for your procurement/legal. Lina, can you attach the whitepaper?
[04:51] Lina (CSM): Yep I'll share the whitepaper and the SOC2 summary after the call.
[04:55] Dr. Elena: On dedicated slots — how fast can you spin those up in our region? We want low lead time for scaling.
[05:01] Samir: Provisioning is typically minutes for extra reserved slots in dedicated capacity, but if you want long-lived committed reserved pools that's part of the Dedicated contract. For the canary we can reserve ephemeral slots.
[05:10] Michael: Can we also see a routing policy that prefers incumbents for fallback vs Redwood variants? I'm just thinking of cost play.
[05:18] Samir: Yes you can configure routing policies — latency-first, cost-first, or hybrid. We can simulate the cost/latency curve in the shared spreadsheet.
[05:25] Ava: Quick demo note — Samir will walk through a short trace where we saw a fallback causing a 120 ms spike. Samir?
[05:30] Samir: Sure, pull up the trace link I posted in chat — (link redacted) — so around timestamp 00:23 of the trace you can see the request routed to a general-purpose variant, kernel switch happens, and p99 spikes. If we pin that session to dedicated, the p99 drops about 80 ms.
[05:48] Dr. Elena: That matches what we see in prod-ish. So for next week we want three experiments: 1) 72h canary with 10% pinned to dedicated slots, 2) run with increased prefix TTL and sticky routing, and 3) full-run on quantized int8 dedicated to validate throughput/cost.
[06:05] Ava: Confirmed — those are the experiments. We'll coordinate the runs and produce a consolidated report.
[06:11] Tom: From procurement perspective, what's the timeline for pricing/contract? We may need 30-day notice for budget window.
[06:17] Ava: We'll send a preliminary pricing delta today and a contract term sheet if the canary metrics look good — aim to have that into your team by the end of next week.
[06:25] Michael: A couple of nitty-grittys — sampling rate for traces (do you sample at 1 in 10 or full?), and can you include GPU kernel-level timing?
[06:33] Samir: We'll push full traces for the benchmark runs (no sampling) and include kernel timing where available. Incumbent traces you'll share.
[06:39] Dr. Elena: Great. One more question: do we expect model-variance when moving from hosted to dedicated to private? Any drift in outputs?
[06:46] Samir: There shouldn't be semantic drift — it's the same model weights and decoding strategy. Differences can come from quantization at extreme low-bits or if fallback variants use different model sizes. We'll keep a quality regression test in the pipeline and run ROUGE/BLEU style checks plus prioritized prompt sets.
[07:01] Rita: Please add an eval run against our golden prompts to the test plan.
[07:05] Ava: Noted.
[07:07] Samir: Quick note on measurement methodology — we'll run p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec, but also report request-level end-to-end time (incl. network) to match your user metrics.
[07:16] Michael: Good.
[07:18] Ava: Any blockers?
[07:20] Dr. Elena: No blockers. We'll send baseline traces and confirm the canary cohort.
[07:24] Tom: I'll review the pricing delta once it's in.
[07:27] Ava: Great. Recap of next steps — Michael sends baseline traces; Samir schedules the dedicated microbench and will run the 72h canary once traces are in; Ava sends pricing delta and spreadsheet today; Lina shares SOC2/whitepaper. We'll reconvene in one week for results.
[07:44] (crosstalk, people saying thanks)
[07:48] Ava: Thanks everyone, meeting adjourned.
